about: Story mode's bottles (docs/loop/items/I-053/spec.md section 5): the codex substance each pack item supplies to a discovered spell. Air supplies its gases free. In the block world a cast of a discovered spell needs a bottle of every reactant and uses up one of each item marked consumed; free play (the Chemistry Bench page) has unlimited bottles. `find` says in plain words where the player gets the item: the missing-bottle caption and the pack show it. Charcoal comes before coal: it is the carbon the story gives (the charcoal clamp), and coal is the alternative. I-057: `from` says how the world gives each item (a stash, the clamp, the rig or the Pick; never by digging), `stashes` are the places bottle items are picked up (walk up to one; it fills again after `refill_s` seconds; a hidden one shows only after a Reveal spell lands near it), and every chemistry quest has a solving reaction whose bottles are all findable (docs/loop/items/I-057/spec.md).

items.find: Heat wood with very little air: cast Fire into the vent on the charcoal mound (Frozen Fields). When the smoke clears, press E there.
Coal works just like charcoal, if you already have some.
Snow covers the Frozen Fields. Point the Pick (key 5) at snowy ground and hold the mouse to scoop some up.
A box of iron nails sits by the workshop in the village. Walk up to it to take some.

items.why: the valley's iron ore is haematite, Fe2O3
items.find: A few rusty brown blocks hide in the rock under the charcoal mound. The Pick (key 5) can pick one up.
Sand lines the river bed at the ford. Point the Pick (key 5) at it and hold the mouse to scoop some up.

items.why: a flask of oxygen; a cast takes a little
items.find: Run the water-splitting rig in the cave (press E there). Each run fills an O2 flask and an H2 balloon.

items.why: a balloon of hydrogen; a cast takes a little
items.find: Run the water-splitting rig in the cave (press E there). Each run fills an H2 balloon and an O2 flask.
White chalk lumps lie at the edge of the marsh hollow, near the gas fire. Walk up to them to take some.

items.why: vinegar is ethanoic (acetic) acid in water
items.find: Vinegar, baking soda and salt sit on a shelf by the house next to the well. Walk up to it to take some.

items.why: baking soda is sodium hydrogencarbonate, NaHCO3
items.find: Baking soda sits on the shelf by the house next to the well, with the vinegar. Walk up to it to take some.

items.why: table salt is sodium chloride, NaCl
items.find: Salt sits on the shelf by the house next to the well, with the vinegar. Walk up to it to take some.

items.why: the blue crystals are copper sulfate (with water locked in them)
items.find: A jar of blue copper sulfate sits by the workshop in the village, next to the iron nails.

items.why: a weak solution of silver nitrate, as in a school lab
items.find: A small dark bottle of silver nitrate stands beside the Formula Bench. It stains skin: only grown-ups use the real one.
